questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Explore new cultures

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: I really wanted to go to the UK and it was important for me to be sure of housing opportunities. I also wanted to go to a student city.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: Very easy. The accommodation was very welcoming with information and they offered a bunch of options for new students such as a campus walking tour and other introduction activities.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: The university offered a pick-up service from the airport, which made transport very easy. My school, the business school, hosted events for exchange students only which provided both information and opportunities to connect with other students.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing through my host institution

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: It was offered to me through the university. It was only a 20 min walk to campus and 5-10 min bike ride so not something that impacted my stay.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: Their accommodations are both on and off campus but for me it made no big difference. I rented a bike through a university service the months I was there for very cheap I think 22pounds.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: There is a difference in the quality of the different accommodations. Mine were older and traditional which meant the conditions and interior design was worse than some of the newer buildings. I got the classical English experience and didn't really bother me.

questions.question: How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: I applied for modules before the summer holiday and I remember the more difficult part was the danish system of what I was allowed to take.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: They were very responsive on their emails. I wrote with some questions for my pre-approval application and reagarding enrolment in post-graduate modules.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: I wanted to take some masters level modules which I wasn't allowed since I was enrolled in the bachelors programme.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Start looking in good time to relieve yourself of time pressure. Also the module codes are labelled with 1,2,3-thousands according to year of study.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Did you take BA or MA classes while you were on exchange *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: The level was lower than at UPCH, which I had expected, since they are not renowned for their economics programmes. I found it pleasant to relax and be able to focus on social events and trips.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: The style was quite different. The lectures were only 1 hour each and fewer than at UCPH. So less contact hours and the seminars had a different structure. It was much more discussion based and relevant to attend. The exams and assignments were more essay based and more focused on critical thinking and discussion rather than problem solving and mathematical methods.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer: Advanced Macroeconomics, Moderns theories of money and monetary policy, Applied econometrics, The international economic environment, Behavioural economics, and introduction to effective decision making.

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: I found Moderns theories of money and monetary policy very interesting but also challenging. The module Behavioural economics was very interesting as well and easy to follow since it didn't have any direct pre-requisites.

What unexpected costs did you encounter? *
questions.answer: I hadn't thought of needing to buy a duvet, plates, cutlery and pans on arrival. We ended up all sharing the kitchen supplies which made it less expensive and wasteful.

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer:
Groceries and coffee out were less expensive than expected. I hadn't formed any expectations about budget and planned on spending accordingly but without restrictions. 
I spent about 1000DKK on travel and trips each month.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: there are over 350 societies at leeds with many different events and possibilities.

questions.question: What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: There is something for everyone.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: I enjoyed some of the events from the music union library, the nordic society and get out get active trips.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: I recommend that you go out in nature on some hikes and see the beautiful landscapes around. Also just try some of the amazing restaurants and student discount options they have at many places. Definitely go on an Otley run ;)

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: not that difficult.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: Join a society or go to their events and chat.

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: The ability to socialise and how chatty many people are out and about.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer: Exchange is what you make it, don't be afraid to ask and talk to people and enjoy your time there.

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: Put yourself out there and Leeds has so many wonderful things to offer.

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: All the great friends and memories I've made.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: Finding a new routine and different communication with your teachers

questions.question: Any other comments?
Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
